source.author: verg
source.text: Ergo exercentur poenis, veterumque malorum supplicia expendunt: aliae panduntur inanes suspensae ad ventos; aliis sub gurgite vasto infectum eluitur scelus, aut exuritur igni; quisque suos patimur Manes; exinde per amplum mittimur Elysium, et pauci laeta arva tenemus; donec longa dies, perfecto temporis orbe, concretam exemit labem, purumque relinquit aetherium sensum atque auraï simplicis ignem.
source.text_original: Ergo exercentur poenis, veterumque malorum / supplicia expendunt: aliae panduntur inanes / suspensae ad ventos; aliis sub gurgite vasto / infectum eluitur scelus, aut exuritur igni; / quisque suos patimur Manes; exinde per amplum / mittimur Elysium, et pauci laeta arva tenemus; / donec longa dies, perfecto temporis orbe, / concretam exemit labem, purumque relinquit / aetherium sensum atque auraï simplicis ignem.
source.text_english: Therefore they are disciplined with punishments and pay the penalties for their old sins: some are hung spread out to the winds, empty; for others their stained guilt is washed away under a vast abyss, or is burned out by fire; each of us suffers his own Manes. Then we are sent through spacious Elysium, and a few of us hold the joyful fields, until in the course of time long days, the completed cycle of time has removed the hardened stain and leaves the ethereal mind pure, and the fire of the simple air.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: i, meus es, iam te in lucos pia turba silentum secretisque ciet volitans pater Aeolus arvis.
reuse.text_original: i, meus es, iam te in lucos pia turba silentum / secretisque ciet volitans pater Aeolus arvis.
reuse.text_english: Go, you are mine; already the dutiful band of the silent summons you to the groves, and Father Aeolus, flying about, calls you to the hidden fields.
